Metadata.title: AgiMate — an AI agent from a ready-made role in a couple of taps
Metadata.description: Pick a ready-made role: skills and instructions are already written. Three steps and the agent answers in chat. Then tune access, channels, your own model, a team, and work with your devices.
Metadata.ogTitle: AgiMate — a working AI agent in a couple of taps
Metadata.ogDescription: Role presets instead of setup from scratch, with tuning when you need it: skills, access rules, channels, your own model, a team of agents, your phone and computer.

hero.title: A working AI agent —
hero.subtitle: Pick a ready-made role: skills and instructions are already written. Three steps and the agent answers in chat. Then tune it as far as you like — access, channels, your own model, a team of agents.

quickStart.title: Three steps to a working agent
quickStart.subtitle: A ready-made role brings its own instructions and skills. Everything it prefills stays editable — before creation and at any point after.

steps.title: Pick a role
steps.description: A gallery of ready-made roles: the description, instructions and matching skills are already written. Or start from scratch if the job is your own.

steps.title: Check the skills
steps.description: The role's skills are already ticked. Drop the ones you don't need, add your own — or just move on and come back to it later.

steps.title: Start talking
steps.description: The agent exists and answers in the dashboard chat. Everything else gets connected when you need it, not before the first message.

quickStart.tuneTitle: And you can always tune it further
tuneItems: Instructions and the set of skills
A team of agents on a shared board

items.title: All or nothing
items.description: The assistant gets access to everything at once — email, files, calendar. One bad tool and the boundaries are gone.

items.title: Black box
items.description: You don't know what the assistant did: which tool it called, with what parameters, what came back. Nothing to investigate with.

items.title: Someone else's model, someone else's bill
items.description: The model was chosen for you, spend is invisible, tokens are resold at a markup. Switching providers isn't an option.

solution.title: An agent you assemble, under rules you set

columns.title: Starts from a ready-made role
columns.description: The preset brings instructions and a set of skills — three steps and the agent answers in chat. None of it is locked: edit before creation and after.

columns.title: You grant the access
columns.description: The agent only sees the connections you bind to it. Inside a connection there are rules: this tool is allowed, this one isn't, this one only with these parameters.

columns.title: Every call in the log
columns.description: Who called what, when, with what result. Denials are logged too — so you can see exactly what the agent tried to do.

tabs.label: Event
tabs.title: An event starts the agent
tabs.description: A message in Telegram or web chat, a scheduled job, a webhook from an external system. AgiMate takes the event and hands it to the agent.

tabs.label: Agent works
tabs.title: The agent picks the right tool
tabs.description: The agent chooses a tool from its skills and connections. Access rules are checked before the call: a forbidden tool never fires, and the attempt stays in the log.

tabs.label: Result
tabs.title: Reply and log entry
tabs.description: The agent replies in the same channel the event came from. The call, its parameters and its result stay in the log — visible in the dashboard.

useCases.title: What you can build today
useCases.subtitle: Scenarios made of parts that already exist in the dashboard — each one shows what it's assembled from

items.title: An agent in Telegram
items.description: Set up a channel: the Telegram connector, an incoming-message trigger, a reply tool. The agent answers per your instructions and the conversation is stored as sessions you can read in the dashboard.

items.title: A scheduled check
items.description: A connector job runs on a schedule: the agent visits an external service, checks what matters and writes to you. Jobs can be paused or run right now.

items.title: Reacting to an event
items.description: An external system sends a webhook — the agent parses the event and takes the next step. Every delivery and every tool call stays in the trigger logs.

items.title: An agent on your device
items.description: The Android and desktop apps are connectors to your own hardware, and there is nowhere else to get them. Notifications, calls and device events become triggers, and the agent answers with a push, spoken text or a command carried out on the device.

items.title: An agent in your IDE
items.description: Over the ACP protocol the agent plugs into your editor and works next to the code — with the same skills, access rules and log as everywhere else.

items.title: Your own service as a tool
items.description: Connect your API as a key-authenticated app or an MCP server — its methods become the agent's tools. What exactly it may do is up to your rules.

items.title: A team of agents on a shared board
items.description: One agent is not the ceiling: assemble a team and give it a shared board. Tasks with statuses, an assigned agent, comments in the thread. Changes reach the dashboard in real time.

items.title: The agent only sees what's bound
items.description: Until a connection is bound to an agent, its tools don't exist for that agent. Bindings are visible from both sides: on the agent and on the connection.

items.title: Rules are checked before the call
items.description: Allow or deny a specific tool, constrain its parameters, close a connection entirely. The rule fires before the external service is ever contacted, and the denial goes to the log.

items.title: Every action logged
items.description: Who called what, when, with what result. Errors and policy denials are collected separately, so you know where to look.

models.title: Your model, your key
models.subtitle: Tokens are billed by your provider at your rate — no markup from us

items.title: Your key at your provider
items.description: Connect a provider with your own key and pay it directly. The model list is pulled from the provider, and unavailable ones are flagged.

items.title: Different models for different jobs
items.description: Chat, vision, image generation — each job gets its own priority list of models. If the first doesn't fit, the next one is used.

items.title: Spend visible in the dashboard
items.description: How many tokens went out, from which agent, on which model. No key of your own yet — start on the platform free tier.

channels.title: Where your agent lives
channels.subtitle: Talk to your agent wherever suits you

integrations.title: What agents connect to
integrations.subtitle: MCP servers and your own API already cover almost anything. The catalog of ready-made integrations keeps growing.

install.title: Your devices as the agent's tools
install.subtitle: The phone and desktop apps are connectors you can't get anywhere else: the agent sees what happens on your hardware and acts on it.

items.title: Android
items.description: An agent on your phone: intercepts notifications, calls, and events — and passes them to your AI agents for processing

items.title: Desktop
items.description: An agent on your computer: monitors files, events, and desktop notifications, executes commands from AI

items.title: n8n
items.description: Build an AI agent with the AgiMate n8n node — it will work for you autonomously

openSource.title: Self-hosted and open code
openSource.description: The platform can be deployed on your own server: data, model keys and logs stay with you. Repositories and deployment instructions are on GitHub; server-side components are opened up as they pass security review.
openSource.selfHosted: Self-hosted — your data and keys stay with you
openSource.audit: Code opened up as it passes security review

meta.title: Terms of Use — AgiMate
meta.description: Terms of use for the AgiMate platform. The document is in progress — the substance is set out here.

Terms.title: Terms of Use
Terms.draftNotice: The final wording will land before public launch. While the document is being prepared, here is the substance — it won't change in spirit.

sections.title: What the service is
sections.body: AgiMate is a platform for building AI agents: you assemble an agent from skills, grant it access to tools, and talk to it through channels.

sections.title: Early access
sections.body: The service runs in early access. Expect occasional downtime, changes in functionality, and limits on usage volume.

sections.title: Your content and keys
sections.body: Agent instructions, conversations, and third-party provider keys belong to you. We use them only to make the service work.

sections.title: Responsibility
sections.body: The agent acts on your instructions, within the boundaries you set. Review your access rules before granting an agent access to sensitive tools.

sections.title: Changes
sections.body: We'll announce changes to these terms on this page and in the community chat.

Terms.contactBody: Write to us in the community chat — we'll answer.

meta.title: Privacy Policy — AgiMate
meta.description: What data AgiMate stores, where keys and logs live. The document is in progress — the substance is set out here.

Privacy.title: Privacy Policy
Privacy.draftNotice: The final wording will land before public launch. While the document is being prepared, here is how things work today.

sections.title: What we store
sections.body: Your OAuth provider profile (name and email address), the agents you create, skills, connections, and your conversations with agents.

sections.title: Tokens and keys
sections.body: The refresh token lives in an HTTP-only cookie and is unreachable from JavaScript. LLM provider keys and connection secrets are stored server-side and are never shown again in the interface.

sections.title: Third-party services
sections.body: Model requests go to the provider whose key you connected. Tool calls go to the services you connected yourself.

sections.title: Logs
sections.body: We keep a log of tool calls and triggers — it exists for your own troubleshooting and is visible in the dashboard.

sections.title: Self-hosted
sections.body: When deployed on your own server, data never leaves your infrastructure.

sections.title: Deletion
sections.body: Write to us and we'll delete your account and the data attached to it.

Privacy.contactBody: Write to us in the community chat — we'll answer.
